title: Why Organ Donation & Millionaire Habits Share One Secret (Defaults)
alt_title_1: The 12% vs 99% Study That Replaces Willpower Forever
alt_title_2: How Behavioral Defaults Automate Wealth and Focus
description_hook: In 2003, behavioral scientists Eric Johnson and Dan Goldstein uncovered why neighboring European nations had 12% vs 99% organ donor consent: a single default checkbox. Here is how to make saving and deep work automatic defaults.

scenes.headline: 12% vs 99%: The Power of One Checkbox
bullets: Nearly identical culture, education, and values
One form design difference changed behavior 8x
scenes.narration: Why did Germany have a twelve-percent organ donor consent rate while neighboring Austria hit ninety-nine percent? One tiny default checkbox.
scenes.source: Johnson & Goldstein, 'Do Defaults Save Lives?', Science (2003)

scenes.headline: Johnson & Goldstein's 2003 'Science' Study
bullets: Germany required checking a box to join (opt-in)
Austria enrolled citizens unless they opted out
scenes.narration: In a 2003 Science paper, psychologists Eric Johnson and Dan Goldstein showed that people rarely change pre-selected options. Germany required citizens to opt in to organ donation; Austria made it opt-out.
scenes.source: Johnson & Goldstein, 'Do Defaults Save Lives?', Science (2003)

scenes.headline: Willpower Collapses; Architecture Doesn't
scenes.left_body: Saving whatever cash is left on Friday night
scenes.right_body: Payday auto-transfers + scheduled 7 AM app blockers
scenes.narration: Most people run their finances and focus backward as opt-in habits - hoping willpower survives at eight PM on Friday to save leftover cash or study.

scenes.headline: Spend 20 Minutes Engineering Your Defaults
scenes.stat_label: ZERO-DECISION SYSTEMS NEVER MISS A REP
scenes.stat_subtext: Automate payday margin • Auto-lock morning deep work
scenes.narration: Millionaire habits work like Austria's form: spend twenty minutes once automating payday savings transfers and morning app blockers so winning happens even when you feel tired.

scenes.headline: Design Once, Compound Automatically
scenes.stat_label: ONE-TIME SETUP BEATS YEARS OF MOTIVATION
bullets: Make good financial behavior the path of least effort
Add deliberate friction to every bad impulse
scenes.narration: Stop relying on fragile daily motivation and engineer automatic opt-out defaults instead, because human psychology already answered the question...
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb (advice, not a study)
